questions.q: A writer has months of notes on a river town and keeps starting drafts that go nowhere. What would McPhee advise first?
choices: Write a summary lede
Work out the structure, ideally by finding an organizing element in the material, before writing the first sentence
Start with an anecdote and see where it goes
Find a resolution, or abandon the story
questions.explain: McPhee wants the shape settled before drafting, and he finds it in the material.

questions.q: Where should structure come from, in McPhee's view?
choices: From the material itself
From a standard template such as three acts
From the editor
From the reader's expectations
questions.explain: He believes each subject suggests its own structure, which is the opposite of template thinking.

questions.q: What solved the structure of The Pine Barrens?
choices: Starting with a summary lede
Writing it in strict chronological order
Cutting it to a short news piece
Realizing that one resident, Fred Brown, connected most of the topics
questions.explain: After about two weeks stuck on a picnic table, McPhee saw that Brown could be the piece's thread.

questions.q: How does 'Travels in Georgia' handle time?
choices: Strictly in order from first day to last
It's organized entirely by theme
It opens partway through with a strong scene, loops back to the beginning, catches up, and continues
It runs in reverse
questions.explain: The structure lets him open strongly without abandoning chronology.

questions.q: What's the main trade-off between chronological and thematic structure?
choices: Chronology is always better
Chronology gives momentum but can bury the best material; theme is clearer but loses forward motion
Thematic order is only for news
There is no trade-off; they are the same
questions.explain: Many of McPhee's pieces combine a chronological spine with thematic sections.

questions.q: Why does McPhee code and sort his notes into sections before writing?
choices: So he can write one section at a time with only its material in front of him
So he can publish the notes as an appendix
So an editor can cut from the bottom
So each section has a kicker
questions.explain: Once structure is fixed and material sorted, each day's writing becomes manageable.

questions.q: Which is a fair criticism of McPhee's approach?
choices: He invents composite characters
He ignores structure
He writes only short news stories
He has more to say about arrangement than about drama: complication, resolution and the people who drive them
questions.explain: Compared with Franklin or Hart, McPhee focuses on arrangement rather than dramatic conflict.

ideas: Know the shape of the whole piece before writing the first sentence, and draw it.
Structure should grow out of the material, not be imposed on it from a template.
Code every note by topic and sort them into the sections of your plan before you draft.
